method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, reverse paraphrase, number-theoretic edge-case review and exact formula/macro/token comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Primitive-recursive divisibility and primality, zero-indexed prime enumeration, bounded construction of the next-prime function, its Euclidean bound, and an integer-division exercise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: x divides y exactly when y is an integer multiple of x, equivalently when some z satisfies xz=y. If a witness exists, a witness no greater than y can be chosen, so bounded existential quantification defines the relation.
samples.checks: The displayed bounded formula is exact. OLCMP-006 corrects the frozen reversed division order, qualifies the remainder test for a positive divisor, and replaces the false every-witness bound by the sufficient bounded-witness statement, including x=y=0.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A prime natural number is neither zero nor one and has only one and itself as divisors. Checking all y at most x gives a bounded universal definition of Prime(x), hence a primitive-recursive relation.
samples.checks: The lower bound x≥2, implication, disjunction and bounded universal range are preserved exactly.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: p(x) is the prime at zero-based position x. Primitive recursion from p(0)=2 and p(x+1)=nextPrime(p(x)) enumerates the primes. nextPrime(x) is the least prime above x, searched only through x factorial plus one, so it is primitive recursive.
samples.checks: Zero indexing, successor recurrence, strict lower bound, inclusive factorial upper bound and the distinction between unbounded computability and bounded primitive recursiveness are all explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For inputs below two, the prime two meets the claimed bound. Otherwise multiply all primes at most x. If p+1 is composite, any prime divisor q of it divides none of those factors, so x<q<p+1; since p≤x factorial, q is at most x factorial plus one.
samples.checks: The Euclidean product, remainder-zero/remainder-one contradiction, strict lower bound and inclusive upper bound remain intact. OLCMP-007 supplies the two omitted small inputs before the frozen product argument.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The problem asks for an integer-division function d(x,y) defined by bounded minimization.
samples.checks: Both the requested operation and the construction method are preserved.
